title: Zero knowledge verification for frontier AI training is possible
abstract: arXiv:2606.05433v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Frontier AI governance frameworks increasingly use cumulative training compute as the primary criterion for designating high-impact models, but enforcement rests on self-reporting because no technical verification primitive for training exists. Any future international agreement on frontier AI faces the same problem at higher stakes: coordinated regulation of technologies with significant externalities has historically rested on technical verification, without which agreements are declaratory. translated_title: 前沿AI训练的零知识验证是可行的
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.05433v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：前沿AI治理框架日益将累积训练计算量作为指定高影响模型的主要标准，但执行依赖于自我报告，因为目前不存在针对训练的技术验证原语。任何未来关于前沿AI的国际协议都面临同样的问题，且风险更高：对具有重大外部性的技术进行协调监管历来依赖于技术验证，没有技术验证的协议仅是宣言性的。最近的治理分析认为零知识证明是一个有前景的候选方案，但在前沿规模上目前不切实际[26, 4]。我们认为这种不切实际是范式限制而非根本性的，并提出了一种针对前沿密集预训练的验证架构，结合预承诺的训练规范、节点间网络观察和中间计算的即时Merkle承诺，通过零知识方式验证。
tldr: 本文提出了一种结合预承诺规范、网络观察和Merkle承诺的零知识验证架构，证明前沿AI训练的可验证性在技术上可行，而非根本不可行。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a zero-knowledge verification architecture combining pre-committed specifications, network observations, and Merkle commitments, demonstrating that verifiability of frontier AI training is technically feasible rather than fundamentally impractical.
